title: Financial Literacy and Financial Well-Being of Nurses of a First-Class Province in the Philippines
authors: Gerzon, R. A.; Lopena, G. L.
tldr: Assesses financial literacy and well-being of 178 nurses in a Philippine province, finding high literacy and great well-being with a significant positive correlation between them.
problem_and_motivation: Financial literacy is critical for financial well-being, but limited research examines this relationship among Filipino healthcare professionals. Nurses face unique financial challenges yet lack targeted financial education.
approach: Used descriptive-correlational design with researcher-made questionnaire.
Sampled 178 nurses using stratified random sampling from a first-class province in the Philippines.
Applied Pearson, Point Biserial, Rank Biserial, and Spearman Rank correlation analyses.
Measured financial literacy and financial well-being levels using Likert-scale instruments.
Analyzed demographic associations with both literacy and well-being.
findings: num: Overall financial literacy was High (M=3.22, SD=0.39) and financial well-being was Great (M=3.03, SD=0.46).
num: Significant positive correlation between financial literacy and financial well-being (rs=0.660, p=0.000).
num: Monthly income was significantly associated with financial literacy (r=0.223, p=0.003).
No significant relationship between demographics and financial well-being.
Higher financial literacy correlates with better financial well-being among nurses.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides empirical data on financial literacy and well-being levels among Filipino nurses. Demonstrates a strong positive correlation between literacy and well-being in this population. Identifies monthly income as the only demographic factor associated with literacy, suggesting structural rather than personal determinants.
directly_justifies: Filipino nurses have high financial literacy and great financial well-being.
Financial literacy and well-being are strongly positively correlated.
Monthly income significantly influences financial literacy levels.
limits: Limited to one province, not nationally representative.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all topic domains (1.A-14.C). Assigned 1.A, 1.B, 1.C high relevance for Filipino professional demographic financial assessment. Rejected algorithmic and system topics (3.A-14.C) as the paper uses descriptive and correlational statistical methods only.

limitations: Single province sample limits generalizability to all Filipino nurses.
Researcher-made questionnaire may have construct coverage gaps.
remember_this: Nurses show high financial literacy and great financial well-being.
Literacy and well-being are strongly positively correlated.
Monthly income is the key demographic factor for literacy.
No demographic link found with financial well-being.
